name: The self-healing chain that leaves a permanent hole -- a transient vendor-auth gap converts into a permanent bronze hole because nothing re-runs after the heal, and every downstream instrument then reads a healthy chain

description: 2026-08-31: cot-rebalancer-runner raised on all 3 invocations (06:00:41/06:01:35/06:03:26Z) with 'rebalancer /auth/token 200 but no access_token -- session TTL expired?'; 0 of 3 bronze feeds landed against 1/5/83 on each of 08-29 and 08-30 (re-derived at 0.0.0_AB_MSTR by s3api with both adjacent dates as controls). The cot .bd.identity cookie then healed UNATTENDED at 11:33:37Z -- inside the runner's own DECLARED 6h tolerance -- and nothing re-ran. The declared tolerance is unreachable by construction: maximum_event_age_in_seconds=21600 beside maximum_retry_attempts=2, which AWS caps at 2 and which exhausted in 165 seconds.

leads: L1 THE CONFIG STATES A TOLERANCE IT CANNOT DELIVER: cot_rebalancer_runner.tf:229 maximum_event_age_in_seconds=21600 (6h) beside :228 maximum_retry_attempts=2. AWS caps async retries at 2 and they back off in minutes -- the three observed invocations spanned 165s. For a function that RAISES, the 6h window is unreachable BY CONSTRUCTION, not misconfigured. An auditor reading the config concludes the opposite of the truth.
L2 THE HEAL WAS INSIDE THE DECLARED WINDOW: secret LastChanged 11:33:37Z vs 06:00Z + 6h = 12:00Z. A policy delivering what the config claims would have caught this with ~27 minutes to spare.

L3 PRIOR ART EXISTS -- smartx-pipeline/assets-pull-onsuccess.tf already chains a daily pull via destination_config{on_success}, and its comments record preserving the async default of 2. Event-chaining need not be invented. ** AMENDED 2026-08-31 by the stage-3 decomp: it need not be PORTED either. The SUBJECT function already carries its own destination_config{on_success} at cot_rebalancer_runner.tf:222-250 @27a3a98cdc (:192 'COMPLETION-KEYED WHOLE-DAY CONVERT'; :199 'on_success the linkage IS the async invocation, unforgeable without it'). Any completion-chained design is an EDIT TO AN EXISTING MECHANISM ON THIS RESOURCE -- build-ladder rung 2, not a cross-pipeline port. **

L4 ** RETRACTED 2026-08-31T19:1xZ by the stage-3 decomp (2.0.0_SA_COO) -- FALSE AT SOURCE. ** It read: 'cot-detection-layer.tf:25 records cot-bd-session-trigger as NOT Terraform-managed (read-only for IAM); ownership must be settled before that design is costed.' The comment at :24-26 heads a `data "aws_secretsmanager_secret"` block and its subject is THE SECRET, not the lambda. cot-bd-session-trigger IS TF-managed: module at cot-pipeline/lambdas.tf:20-37 @9bf20c960b -> resource "aws_lambda_function" at modules/yang-lambda/main.tf:23 @e567ebf4da; live AWS node drift=DECLARED. TWO CARRIERS, ONE CLAIM -- the brief and msg 89883 both cite the same comment line; neither opened lambdas.tf, so this was never corroborated. THERE IS NO OWNERSHIP BLOCKER on a fire-on-heal design.

L4a THE HEAL HAS A DECLARED TF-MANAGED CADENCE (supersedes the 'no cadence in this repo' claim): cot-pipeline/schedule-et.tf:78-97 @16fc99460c, aws_scheduler_schedule cot-bd-session-daily-et, cron(30 7 * * ? *) America/New_York = 11:30Z EDT / 12:30Z EST, target cot-bd-session-trigger {mode: session-refresh}. The observed 11:33:37Z 'unattended heal' WAS that schedule firing on time. Owner lane = 0.6.2_AE_PartnerETL (cot-pipeline/lambdas.tf header), NOT 0.7.0_AE_CloudOps.

L4b ROOT CAUSE REFRAMED -- AN ORDERING DEFECT: the runner fires 06:00Z UTC (cot_rebalancer_runner.tf:171 @27a3a98cdc, still marked PLACEHOLDER pending a WS-4 chain-timing confirm that never happened) which is 5h30m BEFORE its own session's daily mint -- so it runs at the point of MAXIMUM session age (~18.5h) on EVERY day, not just 08-31. 41 of 41 prior days survived because the session's absolute lifetime usually outlasts 18.5h. This adds a build-ladder rung-1 option the brief could not see: MOVE THE FIRE to after the mint. CONSTRAINT: schedule-et.tf:85-88 records the 07:30 ET mint as an Andrew-direct pre-floor placement with an EST-worst-case 54m margin to the 13:30Z floor -- that margin must be re-derived before any replacement time is chosen. The ordering fix is a MITIGATION, not a sufficiency proof; the recovery gap remains separate.

L4c COMPETING ROOT CAUSE, UNDISCRIMINATED AND WITH A DIFFERENT FIX: bd-cot-keepalive (15m) holds READ-only on the secret and extends the session vendor-side; it cannot re-mint. RC-A (absolute session lifetime + worst-moment fire) -> fix the schedule. RC-B (keepalive gapped overnight) -> fix the keepalive. Moving the schedule would MASK RC-B. DISCRIMINATOR, one CloudWatch read and the first thing any TO should carry: did bd-cot-keepalive invoke continuously through the 2026-08-30 -> 08-31 overnight window?

L5 SCOPE IS UNENUMERATED: 70 .tf files carry a schedule_expression (measured, corpus=all) -- that is the CANDIDATE population, not the affected one. 49F carries its own session chain (bd-49f-session-chain.tf), so the SHAPE exists on more than one firm; that is a reason to enumerate, NOT a finding that 49F is affected. The enumeration is a Rule 24 authoring act and is unperformed.
L6 A RECONCILER MUST FIX, NOT NOTIFY -- a detector that only reports is what the standing moratorium forbids without Andrew's word. The line is the deliverable, not the intent.
root_cause: NOT the cookie death, which is transient and self-repairing. The defect is that NOTHING RE-RUNS AFTER THE HEAL: an EventBridge-daily runner with 2 in-minute async retries dies on the day, and the self-repair then makes the gap invisible because every downstream instrument reads a chain that is genuinely healthy. The only wrong thing is a date that does not exist, and nothing asks that question.
